Population increased in Cambridge

The estimated population of Cambridge in 2024 was 149,352 usual residents, a rise of 0.3% since 2023.

This meant that Cambridge's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Cambridge increased by 3%.

Over this slightly longer period, Cambridge was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Cambridge

The average (median) age fell to 31.5 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Cambridge has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Cambridge is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Cambridge's population of 149,352 usual residents was made up of:

  • 21,840 people aged 0 to 15 years, (14.6%)
  • 110,147 people aged 16 to 64 years, (73.7%)
  • 17,365 people aged 65 years and over, (11.6%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Cambridge has a higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (73.7% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Cambridge, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Cambridge
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Cambridge, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 316 people (0.2%). In total, there were 1,158 births and 842 deaths in Cambridge.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 2,894 (-1.9%). There were 18,291 people entering the area and 21,185 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Cambridge's population of 3,098 (2.1%) as a result of 7,439 people entering the area and 4,341 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Cambridge was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Cambridge in mid-2023 is 148,842.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 1,449 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 2,570 people.

Overall, there was an revision downwards of 1,121 people.
